facts.fact: The Registre Social Unique database holds 362,698 households (2,217,518 people) across 99 communes in 10 regions, per the Ministry of Humanitarian Action's representative.
The RSU technical secretary stressed data security and interoperability with the unique identifier to guarantee the authenticity of persons.

facts.fact: The World Bank says the earlier Burkina Naong Sa Ya project helped establish a national social registry of vulnerable households, a platform for expanding and targeting social protection programs, and the new project will support its expanded coverage and use.

note: Deal record only says the project expands the registry and integrates it with IDP and health-insurance databases; no stated service status, programme use or national ID link.

facts.fact: The World Bank SASPP page says the social registry held 344,400 poor households as of June 2025, with roll-out continuing after the safety-net project closed.

note: Subsidies and benefits are named only as services that may require the identifier; no social registry is described.

facts.fact: The minister of family and solidarity said that at 30 June 2026 the RSU database held 433,888 households (over 2 million people, 30% of target) in 110 communes across 12 regions.
The Secrétariat technique du RSU states that 362,818 households (2,220,500 people) were registered in the RSU at 31 December 2025, with the RSU deployed in 99 communes across 10 regions.

systems.owner: Ministère de la Famille et de la Solidarité

facts.fact: leFaso.net reports the Registre Social Unique rollout in Ouahigouya commune, with enumeration from 13 February to 10 March 2025 covering 62,360 households, of which 16,461 poor and vulnerable households (103,312 people) were retained, run by the ST-RSU with WFP support.

facts.fact: The RSU secretariat says the rural pilot in Centre-Ouest and Centre-Est enrolled 143,000 households (about 900,000 people) into the RSU database against 210,440 planned, with scale-up still to come.
